briefs.explicit:
MISSION BRIEF M-005
Units: metres, seconds, kilograms. Time starts at t = 0 when every robot leaves its start location.

Locations (x, y, zone):
- base: (0, 0), outdoor
- warehouse roof: (56, 43), roof
- water tower top: (-107, -145), roof
- electrical room: (-137, 14), indoor
- pump house: (34, 115), indoor
- workcell West: (-92, -105), indoor
- antenna mast: (65, 102), outdoor
- loading dock: (26, 149), outdoor
- parking lot: (-46, -86), outdoor

Robots:
- G1 (rover): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 2 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 21 kg), camera. Endurance: 3780 s, including the return to its start.
- A1 (fixed_arm): installed at workcell West and cannot move; it can only work on tasks located at workcell West. Equipment: robotic arm. Mains-powered (no endurance limit).
- M1 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 7 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 3540 s, including the return to its start.
- D1 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 9 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg). Endurance: 1380 s, including the return to its start.
- D2 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 9.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg), thermal camera. Endurance: 1020 s, including the return to its start.

Tasks:
- T1: Photograph electrical room for the condition report. Location: electrical room. Duration: 90 s. Needs: camera. Deadline: finished by t = 660 s.
- T2: Collect a soil sample (3 kg) at antenna mast and keep it on board. Location: antenna mast. Duration: 90 s. Needs: robotic arm, cargo carrier (payload 3 kg).
- T3: Tighten the valve at electrical room. Location: electrical room. Duration: 240 s. Needs: robotic arm.
- T4: Tighten the valve at parking lot. Location: parking lot. Duration: 270 s. Needs: robotic arm.
- T5: Collect a soil sample (2 kg) at antenna mast and keep it on board. Location: antenna mast. Duration: 150 s. Needs: robotic arm, cargo carrier (payload 2 kg). Deadline: finished by t = 1380 s.
- T6: Deliver the toolkit (1 kg) to pump house. Location: pump house. Duration: 30 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 1 kg). Deadline: finished by t = 420 s.
- T7: Photograph antenna mast for the condition report. Location: antenna mast. Duration: 120 s. Needs: camera. Deadline: finished by t = 240 s.
- T8: Tighten the valve at workcell West. Location: workcell West. Duration: 210 s. Needs: robotic arm. Can start only after T10 is finished.
- T9: Run a thermal scan of parking lot. Location: parking lot. Duration: 90 s. Needs: thermal camera.
- T10: Deliver the toolkit (6 kg) to workcell West. Location: workcell West. Duration: 30 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 6 kg). Deadline: finished by t = 240 s.

Rules:
1. Every task is done by exactly one robot. A robot does its tasks one at a time, in the order you list them, travelling between task locations.
2. A robot can only do a task if it has the needed equipment, enough payload capacity, and can reach the task location.
3. A task that must start after another task waits until that task is finished, even if a different robot does it.
4. Each robot must be back at its start location before its endurance runs out.
5. Every task must be finished by t = 2100 s.

Objective: minimise the finish time of the last task (the makespan).
briefs.informal:
Here's what we need from the robots today.

Positions are in metres from the base at (0, 0). Drones fly straight and can't go indoors; ground robots follow the road grid (so they travel |dx| + |dy|) and can't get onto roofs. Everyone leaves their start spot at time zero.

Places: warehouse roof (56, 43, a rooftop); water tower top (-107, -145, a rooftop); electrical room (-137, 14, indoors); pump house (34, 115, indoors); workcell West (-92, -105, indoors); antenna mast (65, 102, outside); loading dock (26, 149, outside); parking lot (-46, -86, outside).

The fleet: G1 is a rover parked at base that hauls up to 21 kg at 2 m/s and runs for 63 minutes including the drive back. It has a camera. A1 is a robot arm bolted down in workcell West; it can't move but can work on jobs inside workcell West, and it runs on mains power. M1 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 7 kg, moves at 1 m/s and lasts 59 minutes including getting back. D1, a quadcopter waiting at base, carries a camera, cruises at 9 m/s, lifts up to 2 kg and has 23 minutes of flight time, return trip included. D2, a quadcopter waiting at base, carries a camera and a thermal camera, cruises at 9.5 m/s, lifts up to 2 kg and has 17 minutes of flight time, return trip included.

Jobs:
(T1) Document electrical room with pictures - that takes 1.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 11 minutes.
(T2) Pick up a soil sample at antenna mast and keep it on board; it weighs 3 kg - that takes 1.5 minutes on site.
(T3) Someone has to tighten the valve at electrical room - that takes 4 minutes on site.
(T4) The valve at parking lot needs tightening - that takes 4.5 minutes on site.
(T5) Pick up a soil sample at antenna mast and keep it on board; it weighs 2 kg - that takes 2.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 23 minutes.
(T6) Drop the toolkit off at pump house; it weighs 1 kg - that takes 0.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 7 minutes.
(T7) We need pictures of antenna mast for the report - that takes 2 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 4 minutes.
(T8) Someone has to tighten the valve at workcell West - that takes 3.5 minutes on site but only once the toolkit (T10) has arrived.
(T9) Look for overheating equipment around parking lot - that takes 1.5 minutes on site.
(T10) Drop the toolkit off at workcell West; it weighs 6 kg - that takes 0.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 4 minutes.

Everything has to be wrapped up within 35 minutes of the start, and the sooner the last job finishes, the better. Every robot has to make it back to where it started before its battery runs out.
